defmodule LibTmux.Capture do
  @moduledoc """
  Builds a bounded one-shot observation of one existing Linux tmux server.

  Capture checks topology and OS server identity before and after field
  reads. At most two attempts share the original deadline and work budgets;
  `attempts` accepts 1–3. Only inconsistent topology or disappearing read
  targets retry. Decoding and coverage errors remain visible.

  Defaults: 1024 contextual entity rows, 512 commands, 8 MiB total response
  bytes, 64 KiB per response and 5000 ms. Exceeding a ceiling returns an
  error, never a partial success. Linked rows count against the work limit.
  Capture adds no control attachment. Hooks configured on list commands can
  still have effects; retries do not replay application mutations.
  """

  alias LibTmux.{Codec, Command, Deadline, Error, Format, Schema, Server, Snapshot}

  @typedoc """
  Capture-wide budgets shared by all attempts and reads.

  Each read uses the smaller of remaining `max_bytes` and `max_response_bytes`.
  That effective ceiling must fit OneShot's 16 MiB stdout limit. The shared
  deadline must have at most 600,000 ms remaining when OneShot validates a read.
  Invalid combinations raise `ArgumentError` before that command executes.
  """
  @type option ::
          {:timeout, pos_integer()}
          | {:deadline, Deadline.t()}
          | {:attempts, 1..3}
          | {:max_entities | :max_commands | :max_bytes | :max_response_bytes, pos_integer()}
  @session_fields [:id, :attached_count]
  @window_fields [:width, :height, :zoomed]
  @link_fields [:session_id, :index, :window_id, :active]
  @pane_fields [:id, :window_id, :index, :active, :dead, :width, :height, :pid, :exit_status]
  @client_fields [:id, :session_id, :pid, :width, :height, :control_mode]
  @strings %{
    session: [:name],
    window: [:name, :layout],
    pane: [:current_command, :current_path, :title]
  }

  @doc """
  Performs bounded capture through an explicit server descriptor.

  See `t:option/0` for the composed work, response and remaining-deadline
  constraints inherited from `LibTmux.Transport.OneShot.run/3`.
  """
  @spec fetch(Server.t(), [option()]) :: {:ok, Snapshot.t()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def fetch(%Server{} = server, options \\ []) do
    if Keyword.has_key?(options, :deadline) and Keyword.has_key?(options, :timeout),
      do: raise(ArgumentError, "pass a deadline or timeout, not both")

    deadline =
      Keyword.get_lazy(options, :deadline, fn ->
        Deadline.new(Keyword.get(options, :timeout, 5000))
      end)

    options =
      Keyword.validate!(options, [
        :deadline,
        :timeout,
        attempts: 2,
        max_entities: 1024,
        max_commands: 512,
        max_bytes: 8_388_608,
        max_response_bytes: 65_536
      ])

    unless options[:attempts] in 1..3 and
             Enum.all?([:max_entities, :max_commands, :max_bytes, :max_response_bytes], fn key ->
               is_integer(options[key]) and options[key] > 0
             end),
           do:
             raise(
               ArgumentError,
               "capture budgets must be positive integers; attempts must be 1..3"
             )

    state = %{
      server: server,
      deadline: deadline,
      options: Map.new(options),
      commands: 0,
      bytes: 0,
      rows: 0
    }

    attempt(state, 1)
  end

  defp attempt(state, number) do
    try do
      started = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)
      {instance, state} = identity(state)
      {before, state} = topology(state)
      {rows, state} = text_fields(before, state)
      {after_rows, state} = topology(state)
      {after_instance, state} = identity(state)

      if instance != after_instance or signature(before) != signature(after_rows),
        do: stop(state, :topology_changed)

      fields =
        Map.new(Schema.entities(), fn entity -> {entity, Map.keys(Schema.fields(entity))} end)

      case Snapshot.new(rows,
             server_instance: instance,
             captured_from: started,
             captured_until: System.monotonic_time(:millisecond),
             fields: fields,
             complete: Schema.entities()
           ) do
        {:ok, snapshot} ->
          if Deadline.remaining(state.deadline) == 0, do: stop(state, :timeout)
          {:ok, snapshot}

        {:error, error} ->
          throw({:capture_error, error, state})
      end
    catch
      {:capture_error, error, state} ->
        if retryable?(error) do
          if number < state.options.attempts and Deadline.remaining(state.deadline) > 0 do
            attempt(state, number + 1)
          else
            {:error,
             %Error{
               kind: :inconsistent_snapshot,
               phase: :capture,
               details: %{
                 attempts: number,
                 last_kind: error.kind,
                 commands: state.commands,
                 bytes: state.bytes
               }
             }}
          end
        else
          {:error, error}
        end
    end
  end

  defp retryable?(%Error{kind: kind})
       when kind in [
              :topology_changed,
              :inconsistent_snapshot,
              :conflicting_rows,
              :conflicting_link
            ],
       do: true

  defp retryable?(%Error{kind: :command_error, details: %{code: :not_found}}), do: true
  defp retryable?(_error), do: false

  defp topology(state) do
    {sessions, state} = list(state, "list-sessions", [], :session, @session_fields)

    formats =
      Enum.map(@link_fields, &format(:window_link, &1)) ++
        Enum.map(@window_fields, &format(:window, &1))

    {windows, state} = rows(state, "list-windows", ["-a"], Enum.join(formats, "\t"))

    {links_and_windows, state} =
      Enum.map_reduce(windows, state, fn line, acc ->
        fields =
          Enum.map(@link_fields, &{:window_link, &1}) ++ Enum.map(@window_fields, &{:window, &1})

        decoded = decode_row(acc, line, fields)
        link = Map.take(decoded, @link_fields)
        window = decoded |> Map.take(@window_fields) |> Map.put(:id, link.window_id)
        {{link, window}, acc}
      end)

    {panes, state} = list(state, "list-panes", ["-a"], :pane, @pane_fields)
    {clients, state} = list(state, "list-clients", [], :client, @client_fields)
    {links, windows} = Enum.unzip(links_and_windows)

    {%{session: sessions, window: windows, window_link: links, pane: panes, client: clients},
     state}
  end

  defp list(state, command, arguments, entity, fields) do
    expression = Enum.map_join(fields, "\t", &format(entity, &1))
    {lines, state} = rows(state, command, arguments, expression)

    {Enum.map(lines, &decode_row(state, &1, Enum.map(fields, fn field -> {entity, field} end))),
     state}
  end

  defp rows(state, command, arguments, expression) do
    {output, state} = read(state, command, arguments ++ ["-F", expression])

    lines =
      case output do
        "" ->
          []

        _ ->
          unless :binary.last(output) == 10, do: stop(state, :codec_error)
          output |> binary_part(0, byte_size(output) - 1) |> :binary.split("\n", [:global])
      end

    state = %{state | rows: state.rows + length(lines)}

    if state.rows > state.options.max_entities,
      do: stop(state, :resource_limit, %{reason: :entity_rows})

    {lines, state}
  end

  defp decode_row(state, line, fields) do
    values = :binary.split(line, "\t", [:global])
    unless length(values) == length(fields), do: stop(state, :codec_error, %{reason: :row_fields})

    Map.new(Enum.zip(fields, values), fn {{entity, field}, value} ->
      metadata = Schema.field(entity, field)
      {field, decode(state, value <> "\n", metadata, entity, field)}
    end)
  end

  defp decode(state, output, metadata, entity, field) do
    {type, options} =
      case metadata.type do
        {:id, :client} -> {:string, [encoding: :escaped_v1]}
        {:id, _} -> {:string, []}
        :string -> {:string, [encoding: :escaped_v1]}
        :nullable_integer -> {:integer, [min: 0, max: 2_147_483_647]}
        :integer -> {:integer, [min: 0, max: 2_147_483_647]}
        :boolean -> {:boolean, []}
      end

    result =
      if metadata.nullable and output == "\n",
        do: {:ok, nil},
        else: Codec.decode_field(output, type, options)

    case result do
      {:ok, value} ->
        unless Schema.valid_value?(metadata, value),
          do: stop(state, :invalid_field, %{entity: entity, field: field})

        value

      {:error, error} ->
        throw({:capture_error, %{error | path: [entity, field]}, state})
    end
  end

  defp format(entity, field) do
    metadata = Schema.field(entity, field)

    if metadata.type == :string or metadata.type == {:id, :client},
      do: Format.field(metadata.format),
      else: ~S"#{" <> metadata.format <> "}"
  end

  defp text_fields(rows, state) do
    Enum.reduce(@strings, {rows, state}, fn {entity, fields}, {rows, state} ->
      {values, state} =
        rows[entity]
        |> Enum.uniq_by(& &1.id)
        |> Enum.map_reduce(state, fn row, state ->
          Enum.reduce(fields, {row, state}, fn field, {row, state} ->
            {output, state} =
              read(state, "display-message", ["-p", "-t", row.id, format(entity, field)])

            value = decode(state, output, Schema.field(entity, field), entity, field)
            {Map.put(row, field, value), state}
          end)
        end)

      # Merge free-form fields into every contextual row so physical conflicts remain visible.
      by_id = Map.new(values, &{&1.id, Map.take(&1, fields)})
      rows = Map.update!(rows, entity, &Enum.map(&1, fn row -> Map.merge(row, by_id[row.id]) end))
      {rows, state}
    end)
  end

  defp signature(rows) do
    %{
      sessions: rows.session |> Enum.map(& &1.id) |> MapSet.new(),
      links:
        rows.window_link |> Enum.map(&{&1.session_id, &1.index, &1.window_id}) |> MapSet.new(),
      panes: rows.pane |> Enum.map(&{&1.id, &1.window_id}) |> MapSet.new(),
      clients: rows.client |> Enum.map(&{&1.id, &1.session_id}) |> MapSet.new()
    }
  end

  defp identity(state) do
    {output, state} = read(state, "display-message", ["-p", ~S"#{pid}"])

    case Codec.decode_field(output, :integer, min: 1, max: 2_147_483_647) do
      {:ok, pid} ->
        case LibTmux.ProcessIdentity.read(pid) do
          {:ok, token} -> {token, state}
          {:error, _error} -> stop(state, :identity_unavailable)
        end

      {:error, error} ->
        throw({:capture_error, error, state})
    end
  end

  defp read(state, command, arguments) do
    if state.commands >= state.options.max_commands,
      do: stop(state, :resource_limit, %{reason: :commands})

    remaining = state.options.max_bytes - state.bytes
    if remaining <= 0, do: stop(state, :resource_limit, %{reason: :bytes})
    limit = min(remaining, state.options.max_response_bytes)
    state = %{state | commands: state.commands + 1}

    result =
      Server.run(state.server, Command.new(command, arguments),
        deadline: state.deadline,
        max_stdout_bytes: limit,
        max_stderr_bytes: min(limit, 65_536),
        max_total_bytes: limit
      )

    data =
      case result do
        {:ok, data} -> data
        {:error, error} -> error.details
      end

    state = %{
      state
      | bytes:
          state.bytes + byte_size(Map.get(data, :stdout, "")) +
            byte_size(Map.get(data, :stderr, ""))
    }

    if state.bytes > state.options.max_bytes, do: stop(state, :resource_limit, %{reason: :bytes})

    case result do
      {:ok, result} ->
        {result.stdout, state}

      {:error, error} ->
        throw({:capture_error, error, state})
    end
  end

  defp stop(state, kind, details \\ %{}),
    do:
      throw(
        {:capture_error,
         %Error{
           kind: kind,
           phase: :capture,
           details: Map.merge(%{commands: state.commands, bytes: state.bytes}, details)
         }, state}
      )
end

defmodule LibTmux.Codec do
  @moduledoc """
  Decodes bounded field responses and control-output bytes.

  A field response contains one free-form field and one framing newline.
  The default raw mode removes only its framing newline and requires a
  separately qualified raw source. Use `encoding: :escaped_v1` for output
  produced by `LibTmux.Format.field/1`, including tmux 3.4's print path.
  This is a conservative response codec, not a multi-field row codec.
  """

  alias LibTmux.Error

  @typedoc "The required decoded field category; string additionally requires valid UTF-8."
  @type field_type :: :bytes | :string | :integer | :boolean
  @typedoc "Field framing and value validation options; min and max apply only to integer fields."
  @type field_option ::
          {:encoding, :raw | :escaped_v1}
          | {:max_bytes, pos_integer()}
          | {:min | :max, integer() | nil}

  @doc "Removes one framing newline and validates the complete field value."
  @spec decode_field(binary(), :bytes | :string, [field_option()]) ::
          {:ok, binary()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  @spec decode_field(binary(), :integer, [field_option()]) ::
          {:ok, integer()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  @spec decode_field(binary(), :boolean, [field_option()]) ::
          {:ok, boolean()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def decode_field(response, type, options \\ []) when is_binary(response) do
    cond do
      byte_size(response) > max_bytes(options) ->
        error(:resource_limit, :field_bytes)

      byte_size(response) == 0 or :binary.last(response) != 10 ->
        error(:codec_error, :missing_framing_newline)

      true ->
        value = binary_part(response, 0, byte_size(response) - 1)

        with {:ok, value} <- decode_encoding(value, Keyword.get(options, :encoding, :raw)) do
          decode_value(value, type, options)
        end
    end
  end

  @doc "Decodes tmux's three-digit octal output escapes as bytes."
  @spec decode_output(binary(), [{:max_bytes, pos_integer()}]) ::
          {:ok, binary()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def decode_output(value, options \\ []) when is_binary(value) do
    if byte_size(value) > max_bytes(options) do
      error(:resource_limit, :output_bytes)
    else
      output(value, <<>>)
    end
  end

  defp decode_encoding(value, :raw), do: {:ok, value}
  defp decode_encoding(<<"v1:", value::binary>>, :escaped_v1), do: output(value, <<>>)
  defp decode_encoding(_value, :escaped_v1), do: error(:codec_error, :field_marker)
  defp decode_encoding(_value, _encoding), do: raise(ArgumentError, "unknown field encoding")

  defp decode_value(value, :bytes, _options), do: {:ok, value}

  defp decode_value(value, :string, _options) do
    if String.valid?(value), do: {:ok, value}, else: error(:invalid_encoding, :utf8)
  end

  defp decode_value("0", :boolean, _options), do: {:ok, false}
  defp decode_value("1", :boolean, _options), do: {:ok, true}
  defp decode_value(_value, :boolean, _options), do: error(:codec_error, :boolean)

  defp decode_value(value, :integer, options) do
    minimum = Keyword.get(options, :min)
    maximum = Keyword.get(options, :max)

    unless (is_nil(minimum) or is_integer(minimum)) and
             (is_nil(maximum) or is_integer(maximum)) do
      raise ArgumentError, "integer bounds must be integers"
    end

    case Integer.parse(value) do
      {number, ""} ->
        if (is_nil(minimum) or number >= minimum) and (is_nil(maximum) or number <= maximum),
          do: {:ok, number},
          else: error(:codec_error, :integer_range)

      _ ->
        error(:codec_error, :integer)
    end
  end

  defp decode_value(_value, _type, _options), do: raise(ArgumentError, "unknown field type")

  defp output(<<>>, decoded), do: {:ok, decoded}

  defp output(<<92, a, b, c, rest::binary>>, decoded)
       when a in ?0..?3 and b in ?0..?7 and c in ?0..?7 do
    byte = (a - ?0) * 64 + (b - ?0) * 8 + c - ?0
    output(rest, <<decoded::binary, byte>>)
  end

  defp output(<<byte, rest::binary>>, decoded) when byte >= 32 and byte != 92 do
    output(rest, <<decoded::binary, byte>>)
  end

  defp output(_value, _reversed), do: error(:invalid_encoding, :output_escape)

  defp max_bytes(options) do
    case Keyword.get(options, :max_bytes, 1_048_576) do
      value when is_integer(value) and value > 0 -> value
      _ -> raise ArgumentError, "max_bytes must be a positive integer"
    end
  end

  defp error(kind, reason) do
    {:error, %Error{kind: kind, phase: :capture, details: %{reason: reason}}}
  end
end

defmodule LibTmux.Command do
  @moduledoc """
  A command value with separate argv and tmux-text renderers.

  Construction performs no I/O. Arguments are bytes without NUL. Rendering
  protects command syntax; arguments interpreted as formats still require
  `LibTmux.Format`. A command value does not authorize a shared control lane
  or establish completion behavior, including configured hooks and aliases.
  """

  @enforce_keys [:name, :args]
  defstruct [:name, :args]

  @typedoc "Trusted command data without I/O. Format operands need separate encoding before execution."
  @opaque t :: %__MODULE__{name: String.t(), args: [binary()]}
  @typedoc "A positive byte ceiling for the selected argv or text rendering; encoded output is charged separately."
  @type option :: {:max_bytes, pos_integer()}

  @doc "Constructs a trusted command, rejecting invalid arguments and input size."
  @spec new(String.t(), [binary()], [option()]) :: t()
  def new(name, args, options \\ []) do
    limit = limit(options)

    unless is_binary(name) and byte_size(name) in 1..64 and
             Regex.match?(~r/\A[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*\z/, name) and is_list(args) and
             length(args) <= 1024 and Enum.all?(args, &argument?/1) do
      raise ArgumentError,
            "command requires a valid name and at most 1024 NUL-free binary arguments"
    end

    ensure_size!([name | args], limit)
    %__MODULE__{name: name, args: args}
  end

  @doc "Returns process arguments, preserving terminal semicolons in tmux's argv parser."
  @spec argv(t(), [option()]) :: [binary()]
  def argv(%__MODULE__{name: name, args: args}, options \\ []) do
    _ = new(name, args, options)
    result = [name | Enum.map(args, &argv_argument/1)]
    ensure_size!(result, limit(options))
    result
  end

  @doc "Renders one newline-free tmux command line within its encoded byte budget."
  @spec render(t(), [option()]) :: binary()
  def render(%__MODULE__{name: name, args: args}, options \\ []) do
    _ = new(name, args, options)

    size =
      byte_size(name) +
        Enum.reduce(args, 0, fn value, size -> size + 3 + 4 * byte_size(value) end)

    if size > limit(options), do: raise(ArgumentError, "encoded command exceeds max_bytes")

    [name | Enum.map(args, fn value -> [" ", quote_argument(value)] end)]
    |> IO.iodata_to_binary()
  end

  defp quote_argument(value) do
    [
      "\"",
      for(<<byte <- value>>,
        do: ["\\", byte |> Integer.to_string(8) |> String.pad_leading(3, "0")]
      ),
      "\""
    ]
  end

  defp argv_argument(value) do
    if byte_size(value) > 0 and :binary.last(value) == ?; do
      binary_part(value, 0, byte_size(value) - 1) <> "\\;"
    else
      value
    end
  end

  defp argument?(value), do: is_binary(value) and :binary.match(value, <<0>>) == :nomatch

  defp ensure_size!(arguments, limit) do
    size = Enum.reduce(arguments, 0, fn argument, size -> size + byte_size(argument) + 1 end)
    if size > limit, do: raise(ArgumentError, "command exceeds max_bytes")
  end

  defp limit(options) do
    case Keyword.get(options, :max_bytes, 65_536) do
      value when is_integer(value) and value > 0 -> value
      _ -> raise ArgumentError, "max_bytes must be a positive integer"
    end
  end
end

defmodule LibTmux.Control do
  @moduledoc """
  A connection handle pinned to one qualified control epoch.

  `submit/3` returns a retained `LibTmux.Operation` after bounded admission.
  It never retries, refreshes, attaches, creates sessions or changes transport.
  `request_close/1` closes write authority for the entire pinned epoch through
  reserved capacity; it does not prove retirement or roll back effects.

  `start_link/1` explicitly attaches to an existing session. Its host must qualify
  the server's effective hooks, aliases and stream writers for the whole lane;
  a pinned handle is not authentication against unqualified command output or
  arbitrary writes to internal tables. Reads and local selections never attach.
  """

  alias LibTmux.{Deadline, Error, Operation}
  alias LibTmux.Control.{Admission, Exchange, Inbox, Lifetime, Records, Request, Start}

  @enforce_keys [:owner, :view, :lifetime, :endpoint]
  @derive {Inspect, only: []}
  defstruct @enforce_keys
  @typedoc "A handle pinned to one owner and connection epoch; it never follows a replacement."
  @opaque t :: %__MODULE__{}

  @typedoc "Explicit attachment policy and bounded startup settings; capacities count slots and timeouts use milliseconds."
  @type start_option ::
          {:server, LibTmux.Server.t()}
          | {:session, {:existing, String.t()}}
          | {:lane, :host_qualified}
          | {:timeout, 1..600_000}
          | {:capacity | :metadata_capacity | :waiter_capacity, 1..256}
          | {:retention_ms, 1..600_000}

  @typedoc "A positive millisecond budget shared by all stages of one lifecycle or submission call."
  @type call_option :: {:timeout, pos_integer()}

  @typedoc "A pinned epoch's current phase and identity; retirement and unknown cleanup are distinct."
  @type connection_status :: %{
          epoch: reference() | nil,
          generation: non_neg_integer(),
          phase: :starting | :ready | :closing | :retired | :unknown,
          instance: String.t() | nil
        }

  @doc """
  Starts a linked connection and returns `{:ok, root, control}`.

  Require `server: %LibTmux.Server{}`, `session: {:existing, "$id"}` and
  `lane: :host_qualified`. No session is created. The attachment is visible in
  tmux's client counts and can update session state. `no-output,ignore-size`
  suppresses pane output and excludes this client from window sizing.

  `timeout` defaults to 5000ms and accepts 1..600000ms. One budget covers input
  preparation, Root startup, bootstrap, ready waiting and handoff. A fresh
  factory returns a ready handle. Runtime failures return a structured error;
  invalid trusted options raise `ArgumentError`. Ordinary OTP links remain:
  an asynchronous fatal Root exit can terminate a non-trapping caller.

  Failed startup fences its lifetime and requests exact-Root cleanup. Error
  details distinguish observed Root exit from a kill request; unknown native
  cleanup is never success. OTP can await Root exit after its initialization
  timer expires, so a strict wall-clock caller-return bound remains unqualified.

  Optional `capacity`, `metadata_capacity` and `waiter_capacity` default to 32
  and accept 1..256. `retention_ms` defaults to 60000 and accepts 1..600000.

  Ready connections buffer at most 64 KiB or 128 stdout chunks behind the
  reader. Overflow closes the whole epoch with `resource_limit`; it never
  replays commands. These receive limits do not cap borrowed-server memory.
  """
  @spec start_link([start_option()]) :: {:ok, pid(), t()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def start_link(options) do
    entered_at = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)
    Start.start(options, entered_at)
  end

  @doc """
  Builds a permanent supervisor child spec without attaching.

  Prepares bounded detached inputs and one lifetime shared by all factory
  invocations. Each invocation starts its own configured startup budget.
  A restarted nonfresh lifetime returns an inert handle and never attaches
  automatically. Proven retirement permits explicit `reconnect/2`; unknown
  cleanup refuses it. Old handles never follow a replacement Root or Manager.

  `Supervisor.start_child/2` and `Supervisor.restart_child/2` return the new
  handle as their third info element. After an automatic restart, use
  `Supervisor.terminate_child/2` followed by `Supervisor.restart_child/2` for
  fresh info. This does not clear unknown cleanup or authorize replay.
  """
  @spec child_spec([start_option()]) :: Supervisor.child_spec()
  def child_spec(options), do: Start.child_spec(options)

  @doc false
  def from_descriptor(%{owner: owner, view: view, lifetime: lifetime}) do
    with {:ok, endpoint} <- read(owner, view, lifetime),
         :ok <- ready(endpoint),
         {:ok, _template} <- Operation.prepare(endpoint) do
      {:ok, %__MODULE__{owner: owner, view: view, lifetime: lifetime, endpoint: endpoint}}
    end
  end

  @doc false
  def from_start_descriptor(%{owner: owner, view: view, lifetime: lifetime}) do
    with {:ok, endpoint} <- read(owner, view, lifetime),
         true <-
           endpoint.records.pool === endpoint.pool and endpoint.pool.owner == endpoint.manager,
         true <-
           endpoint.inbox.owner == endpoint.manager and
             :connection in endpoint.inbox.kinds and
             endpoint.waiter_inbox.owner == endpoint.manager and
             :await in endpoint.waiter_inbox.kinds,
         :ok <- Records.validate(endpoint.records),
         :ok <- Inbox.validate(endpoint.inbox),
         :ok <- Inbox.validate(endpoint.waiter_inbox) do
      {:ok, %__MODULE__{owner: owner, view: view, lifetime: lifetime, endpoint: endpoint}}
    else
      false -> failure(:wrong_connection)
      error -> error
    end
  end

  @doc false
  def await_ready(%__MODULE__{endpoint: endpoint} = control, %Deadline{} = deadline) do
    with {:ok, acknowledged} <-
           Exchange.call(endpoint.inbox, endpoint.epoch, deadline, {:connection, :ready}),
         do: bind_reconnected(control, acknowledged)
  end

  @doc """
  Admits one request and returns its retained operation handle.

  `timeout` defaults to 5000ms and covers validation, admission, queueing,
  writes and replies under one monotonic deadline. Request binaries are
  detached before publication. Invalid input, overload or stale context before
  admission returns a no-write error. Every successful admission returns its
  Operation, even if its context disappears before publication. Inspect that
  handle for the eventual canonical result or an explicit lost-context error.

  Closing the connection can affect sibling operations. Command replies do
  not prove external program exit. Caller timeout does not authorize replay.
  """
  @spec submit(t(), Request.t(), [call_option()]) :: {:ok, Operation.t()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def submit(%__MODULE__{} = control, %Request{} = request, options \\ []) do
    entered_at = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)
    options = Keyword.validate!(options, timeout: 5000)
    deadline = Deadline.new(options[:timeout], now: entered_at)

    with :ok <- unexpired(deadline),
         {:ok, endpoint} <- current(control),
         :ok <- ready(endpoint),
         {:ok, request, line} <- Request.prepare(request, endpoint.instance),
         {:ok, template} <- Operation.prepare(endpoint),
         {:ok, lease} <-
           Admission.claim(
             endpoint.pool,
             endpoint.epoch,
             endpoint.router,
             deadline,
             byte_size(line)
           ) do
      %Operation{} = operation = Operation.bind(template, lease)
      publish(control, endpoint, lease, request, deadline)
      {:ok, operation}
    else
      {:error, %Error{} = error} -> {:error, %{error | certainty: :no_write}}
      {:error, _reason} -> failure(:resource_limit)
    end
  end

  @doc "Admits a request or raises the same structured error."
  @spec submit!(t(), Request.t(), [call_option()]) :: Operation.t()
  def submit!(control, request, options \\ []), do: unwrap(submit(control, request, options))

  @doc "Reads the pinned epoch's current phase and identity without contacting tmux."
  @spec status(t()) :: {:ok, connection_status()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def status(%__MODULE__{} = control) do
    result =
      with {:ok, endpoint} <- current(control) do
        %{generation: generation, phase: phase} = Lifetime.status(control.lifetime)

        if generation == endpoint.generation do
          {:ok,
           %{
             epoch: endpoint.epoch,
             generation: generation,
             phase: phase,
             instance: endpoint.instance
           }}
        else
          failure(:stale_connection)
        end
      end

    case result do
      {:error, %Error{} = error} -> {:error, %{error | phase: :status, certainty: :unknown}}
      success -> success
    end
  end

  @doc "Reads pinned connection status or raises the same structured error."
  @spec status!(t()) :: connection_status()
  def status!(control), do: unwrap(status(control))

  @doc """
  Requests whole-epoch closure without claiming an operation or metadata slot.

  Repeated requests for the same closing or proven-retired generation return
  `:ok`. Success is a request or previously known retirement, not a cleanup
  acknowledgement. A replacement Manager or epoch is never followed.
  """
  @spec request_close(t()) :: :ok | {:error, Error.t()}
  def request_close(%__MODULE__{} = control) do
    result =
      with {:ok, endpoint} <- current(control) do
        case Lifetime.status(control.lifetime) do
          %{generation: generation, phase: :retired} when generation == endpoint.generation ->
            :ok

          %{generation: 0, phase: :unknown} ->
            failure(:cleanup_unknown)

          _ ->
            Lifetime.revoke(control.lifetime, endpoint.generation)
        end
      end

    case result do
      {:error, %Error{} = error} -> {:error, %{error | phase: :close, certainty: :unknown}}
      :ok -> :ok
    end
  end

  @doc "Requests epoch closure or raises the same structured error."
  @spec request_close!(t()) :: :ok
  def request_close!(control), do: unwrap(request_close(control))

  @doc """
  Requests closure and waits for proven retirement of the pinned epoch.

  `timeout` defaults to 5000ms. The original budget includes validation and
  retirement waiting. Closure still happens if the bounded metadata wait cannot
  be admitted. Timeout, overload or lost ownership reports unknown certainty;
  it never proves cleanup. `:ok` requires known native and actor retirement.

  The connection supervisor and retained records remain available for explicit
  reconnect and inspection. This does not stop the supervisor or roll back
  sibling effects.
  """
  @spec close(t(), [call_option()]) :: :ok | {:error, Error.t()}
  def close(%__MODULE__{} = control, options \\ []) do
    deadline = lifecycle_deadline(options)

    result =
      with :ok <- request_close(control),
           {:ok, endpoint} <- current(control) do
        case Lifetime.status(control.lifetime) do
          %{generation: generation, phase: :retired} when generation == endpoint.generation ->
            unexpired(deadline)

          _ ->
            Exchange.call(endpoint.inbox, endpoint.epoch, deadline, {:connection, :retired})
        end
      end

    lifecycle_result(result, :close)
  end

  @doc "Waits for retirement or raises the same structured error."
  @spec close!(t(), [call_option()]) :: :ok
  def close!(control, options \\ []), do: unwrap(close(control, options))

  @doc """
  Explicitly obtains the ready epoch, starting a replacement only after retirement.

  A ready epoch returns itself. Call `close/2` first to require replacement.
  The default 5000ms budget covers metadata admission, retirement and startup.
  A successful reply pins the acknowledged endpoint even if it becomes stale
  before this caller resumes. It never follows a later view or replays work.
  Errors report unknown certainty about existing effects. Attachment counts
  include the control client; reconnect can attach one replacement client.
  """
  @spec reconnect(t(), [call_option()]) :: {:ok, t()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def reconnect(%__MODULE__{} = control, options \\ []) do
    deadline = lifecycle_deadline(options)

    result =
      with {:ok, endpoint} <- current(control),
           {:ok, acknowledged} <-
             Exchange.call(endpoint.inbox, endpoint.epoch, deadline, {:reconnect, nil}) do
        bind_reconnected(control, acknowledged)
      end

    lifecycle_result(result, :connect)
  end

  @doc "Obtains the ready epoch or raises the same structured error."
  @spec reconnect!(t(), [call_option()]) :: t()
  def reconnect!(control, options \\ []), do: unwrap(reconnect(control, options))

  defp bind_reconnected(control, acknowledged) do
    shared = [:manager, :pool, :records, :inbox, :waiter_inbox, :lifetime]
    original = control.endpoint

    epoch_matches =
      (acknowledged.generation == original.generation and acknowledged.epoch == original.epoch) or
        (acknowledged.generation == original.generation + 1 and
           acknowledged.epoch != original.epoch)

    if acknowledged.phase == :ready and epoch_matches and
         Map.take(acknowledged, shared) === Map.take(original, shared),
       do: {:ok, %{control | endpoint: acknowledged}},
       else: failure(:invalid_reply)
  end

  defp lifecycle_deadline(options) do
    entered_at = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)
    options = Keyword.validate!(options, timeout: 5000)
    Deadline.new(options[:timeout], now: entered_at)
  end

  defp lifecycle_result({:error, %Error{} = error}, phase),
    do: {:error, %{error | phase: phase, certainty: :unknown}}

  defp lifecycle_result(result, _phase), do: result

  defp publish(control, endpoint, lease, request, deadline) do
    with {:ok, ^endpoint} <- current(control),
         :ok <- ready(endpoint),
         {:ok, :reserved} <- Admission.state(endpoint.pool, lease),
         true <- Deadline.remaining(deadline) > 0 do
      send(endpoint.router, {:submit, endpoint.epoch, lease, request})
    end

    :ok
  end

  defp current(control) do
    with {:ok, endpoint} <- read(control.owner, control.view, control.lifetime) do
      if Map.drop(endpoint, [:phase, :births]) === Map.drop(control.endpoint, [:phase, :births]),
        do: {:ok, endpoint},
        else: failure(:stale_connection)
    end
  end

  defp read(owner, view, lifetime) do
    case :ets.info(view, :owner) do
      :undefined ->
        failure(:connection_lost)

      ^owner ->
        with [{:context, %{owner: ^owner, lifetime: ^lifetime}}] <- :ets.lookup(view, :context),
             [{:connection, %{lifetime: ^lifetime, manager: manager} = endpoint}] <-
               :ets.lookup(view, :connection),
             true <- Process.alive?(owner) and Process.alive?(manager) do
          {:ok, endpoint}
        else
          _ -> failure(:stale_connection)
        end

      _ ->
        failure(:wrong_connection)
    end
  rescue
    ArgumentError -> failure(:connection_lost)
  end

  defp ready(%{phase: :ready} = endpoint) do
    if Lifetime.allows_write?(endpoint.lifetime, endpoint.generation),
      do: :ok,
      else: failure(:stale_epoch)
  end

  defp ready(_endpoint), do: failure(:not_ready)

  defp unexpired(deadline),
    do: if(Deadline.remaining(deadline) > 0, do: :ok, else: failure(:timeout))

  defp failure(kind), do: {:error, %Error{kind: kind, phase: :admission, certainty: :no_write}}
  defp unwrap({:ok, value}), do: value
  defp unwrap({:error, error}), do: raise(error)
  defp unwrap(:ok), do: :ok
end

defmodule LibTmux.Format do
  @moduledoc """
  Constructs literal operands for tmux formats without evaluating their text.

  Command quoting and format quoting are separate. A literal may contain
  newlines or arbitrary non-NUL bytes; this does not qualify its output for
  a shared line-oriented control lane.
  """

  @syntax_bytes [35, 123, 125, 44, 58, 59]

  @field_modifiers Enum.map_join([92, 36 | Enum.to_list(1..31) ++ [127]], ";", fn byte ->
                     pattern =
                       case byte do
                         92 -> "\\\\"
                         36 -> "\\$"
                         _ -> <<byte>>
                       end

                     replacement =
                       "\\\\" <> (byte |> Integer.to_string(8) |> String.pad_leading(3, "0"))

                     "s|" <> pattern <> "|" <> replacement <> "|"
                   end)

  @doc """
  Encodes one named field for `LibTmux.Codec.decode_field/3` with `encoding: :escaped_v1`.

  Backslashes are replaced first, then dollars and ASCII control bytes.
  This protects values from tmux 3.4's ambiguous print escaping. The `v1:`
  prefix and encoded newlines prevent field text from becoming reply guards.
  This is one field per response, not a delimiter-framed row or arbitrary
  format wrapper. The caller must still bound the response and validate the
  field against its schema and the connected server's capabilities.
  """
  @spec field(String.t()) :: binary()
  def field(name) when is_binary(name) do
    unless byte_size(name) in 1..64 and Regex.match?(~r/\A@?[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\z/, name),
      do: raise(ArgumentError, "field must be a tmux variable or named user option")

    "v1:" <> ~S"#{" <> @field_modifiers <> ":" <> name <> "}"
  end

  @doc "Returns a format expression that expands to exactly the supplied non-NUL bytes."
  @spec literal(binary()) :: binary()
  def literal(value) when is_binary(value) do
    if :binary.match(value, <<0>>) != :nomatch do
      raise ArgumentError, "tmux format literals cannot contain NUL"
    end

    for <<byte <- value>>, into: "" do
      if byte in @syntax_bytes do
        ~S"#{a:" <> Integer.to_string(byte) <> "}"
      else
        <<byte>>
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule LibTmux.Protocol do
  @moduledoc """
  Assembles bounded control-mode replies and lexical notifications from bytes.

  Reply guards retain timestamp, command number and flags. Inside a block,
  notification-looking output stays data. The parser cannot authenticate
  injected matching guards: shared lanes must separately qualify commands,
  hooks and subscription expansion. Notification payloads need semantic
  validation before they can update a graph.

  A parse error retains already completed events in `error.details.events`.
  Its owner must retire the lane rather than reuse the rejected state.
  """

  alias LibTmux.Error

  @limits %{
    max_chunk_bytes: 65_536,
    max_line_bytes: 65_536,
    max_frame_bytes: 262_144,
    max_frame_lines: 4096,
    max_events: 1024
  }

  @notifications %{
    "client-detached" => :client_detached,
    "client-session-changed" => :client_session_changed,
    "config-error" => :config_error,
    "continue" => :continue,
    "exit" => :exit,
    "extended-output" => :extended_output,
    "layout-change" => :layout_change,
    "message" => :message,
    "output" => :output,
    "pane-mode-changed" => :pane_mode_changed,
    "pause" => :pause,
    "session-changed" => :session_changed,
    "session-renamed" => :session_renamed,
    "session-window-changed" => :session_window_changed,
    "sessions-changed" => :sessions_changed,
    "subscription-changed" => :subscription_changed,
    "unlinked-window-add" => :unlinked_window_add,
    "unlinked-window-close" => :unlinked_window_close,
    "unlinked-window-renamed" => :unlinked_window_renamed,
    "window-add" => :window_add,
    "window-close" => :window_close,
    "window-pane-changed" => :window_pane_changed,
    "window-renamed" => :window_renamed
  }

  defstruct carry: "", guard: nil, lines: [], frame_bytes: 0, frame_lines: 0, limits: @limits

  @typedoc "A complete tmux reply guard: timestamp, command number and flags, retained for correlation."
  @type guard_id :: {non_neg_integer(), non_neg_integer(), non_neg_integer()}
  @typedoc "A framed reply or lexical notification. Payloads still require semantic validation before graph updates."
  @type event ::
          {:reply, :ok | :error, guard_id(), [binary()]}
          | {:notification, atom(), binary()}
          | {:unknown, binary()}
  @typedoc "Immutable parser carry and bounded in-flight frame state; discard it after any parse error."
  @opaque t :: %__MODULE__{}
  @typedoc "A positive parser ceiling, measured in bytes, lines or emitted events as named."
  @type option ::
          {:max_chunk_bytes | :max_line_bytes | :max_frame_bytes | :max_frame_lines | :max_events,
           pos_integer()}

  @doc "Constructs a parser with positive byte, line and event limits."
  @spec new([option()]) :: t()
  def new(options \\ []) do
    limits = options |> Keyword.validate!(Map.to_list(@limits)) |> Map.new()

    Enum.each(limits, fn {key, value} ->
      unless is_integer(value) and value > 0,
        do: raise(ArgumentError, "#{key} must be a positive integer")
    end)

    %__MODULE__{limits: limits}
  end

  @doc "Consumes one byte chunk without performing I/O."
  @spec feed(t(), binary()) :: {:ok, [event()], t()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def feed(%__MODULE__{} = state, chunk) when is_binary(chunk) do
    if byte_size(chunk) > state.limits.max_chunk_bytes do
      error(:resource_limit, :chunk_bytes, [])
    else
      parse(%{state | carry: ""}, state.carry <> chunk, [], 0)
    end
  end

  @doc "Rejects a stream ending inside a line or reply block."
  @spec finish(t()) :: :ok | {:error, Error.t()}
  def finish(%__MODULE__{carry: "", guard: nil}), do: :ok
  def finish(%__MODULE__{}), do: error(:protocol_error, :truncated_stream, [])

  defp parse(state, buffer, events, count) do
    case :binary.match(buffer, "\n") do
      :nomatch ->
        if byte_size(buffer) > state.limits.max_line_bytes,
          do: error(:resource_limit, :line_bytes, events),
          else: {:ok, Enum.reverse(events), %{state | carry: :binary.copy(buffer)}}

      {size, 1} ->
        if size > state.limits.max_line_bytes do
          error(:resource_limit, :line_bytes, events)
        else
          <<line::binary-size(^size), 10, rest::binary>> = buffer

          case line(state, line) do
            {:ok, next, nil} ->
              parse(next, rest, events, count)

            {:ok, _next, _event} when count >= state.limits.max_events ->
              error(:resource_limit, :events, events)

            {:ok, next, event} ->
              parse(next, rest, [event | events], count + 1)

            {:error, kind, reason} ->
              error(kind, reason, events)
          end
        end
    end
  end

  defp line(%{guard: nil} = state, line) do
    case guard(line) do
      {:ok, "%begin", id} ->
        {:ok, %{state | guard: id}, nil}

      {:ok, _end, _id} ->
        {:error, :protocol_error, :unexpected_guard}

      :invalid ->
        {:error, :protocol_error, :invalid_guard}

      :none ->
        {:ok, state, notification(line)}
    end
  end

  defp line(state, line) do
    case guard(line) do
      {:ok, kind, id} when kind in ["%end", "%error"] and id == state.guard ->
        status = if kind == "%end", do: :ok, else: :error
        event = {:reply, status, id, Enum.reverse(state.lines)}
        {:ok, %{state | guard: nil, lines: [], frame_bytes: 0, frame_lines: 0}, event}

      _ ->
        bytes = state.frame_bytes + byte_size(line) + 1
        lines = state.frame_lines + 1

        if bytes > state.limits.max_frame_bytes or lines > state.limits.max_frame_lines do
          {:error, :resource_limit, :frame_size}
        else
          {:ok,
           %{
             state
             | lines: [:binary.copy(line) | state.lines],
               frame_bytes: bytes,
               frame_lines: lines
           }, nil}
        end
    end
  end

  defp guard(line) do
    case :binary.split(line, " ") do
      [kind, rest] when kind in ["%begin", "%end", "%error"] and byte_size(rest) <= 62 ->
        guard_values(kind, rest)

      [kind | _] when kind in ["%begin", "%end", "%error"] ->
        :invalid

      _ ->
        :none
    end
  end

  defp guard_values(kind, rest) do
    case :binary.split(rest, " ", [:global]) do
      [time, number, flags] ->
        with {:ok, time} <- unsigned(time),
             {:ok, number} <- unsigned(number),
             {:ok, flags} <- unsigned(flags) do
          {:ok, kind, {time, number, flags}}
        else
          _ -> :invalid
        end

      _ ->
        :invalid
    end
  end

  defp unsigned(value) when byte_size(value) in 1..20 do
    if Enum.all?(:binary.bin_to_list(value), &(&1 in ?0..?9)),
      do: {:ok, String.to_integer(value)},
      else: :invalid
  end

  defp unsigned(_value), do: :invalid

  defp notification(<<"%", body::binary>> = raw) do
    [name | rest] = :binary.split(body, " ")

    case Map.fetch(@notifications, name) do
      {:ok, name} -> {:notification, name, Enum.at(rest, 0, "") |> :binary.copy()}
      :error -> {:unknown, :binary.copy(raw)}
    end
  end

  defp notification(raw), do: {:unknown, :binary.copy(raw)}

  defp error(kind, reason, events) do
    {:error,
     %Error{
       kind: kind,
       phase: :parse,
       path: [:control],
       details: %{reason: reason, events: Enum.reverse(events)}
     }}
  end
end

defmodule LibTmux.Snapshot do
  @moduledoc """
  An indexed immutable graph observed over a capture interval.

  Construction and traversal perform no I/O. `fields` declares loaded fields
  over the supplied entity IDs; `complete` declares complete server entity
  sets. Missing declarations remain unloaded, including on empty sets.
  Unavailable capabilities use a separate declaration. Relations require
  complete join domains. A snapshot reserves no tmux objects.
  """

  alias LibTmux.{Error, Ref, Schema}

  @collections %{
    session: :sessions,
    window: :windows,
    window_link: :window_links,
    pane: :panes,
    client: :clients
  }
  @foreign_keys %{
    pane: [window_id: :window],
    window_link: [session_id: :session, window_id: :window],
    client: [session_id: :session]
  }
  @enforce_keys [:id, :server_instance, :captured_from, :captured_until, :coverage]
  defstruct [
    :id,
    :server_instance,
    :captured_from,
    :captured_until,
    :coverage,
    schema_version: 1,
    sessions: %{},
    windows: %{},
    window_links: %{},
    panes: %{},
    clients: %{},
    order: %{},
    indexes: %{}
  ]

  @typedoc "Coverage of one captured entity domain; missing field entries are unloaded."
  @type entity_coverage :: %{
          ids: MapSet.t(Ref.id()),
          complete: boolean(),
          fields: %{optional(atom()) => :loaded | :unavailable}
        }
  @typedoc "Declared entity sets and field availability; completeness is separate from an empty captured set."
  @type coverage :: %{entities: %{Schema.entity() => entity_coverage()}}
  @typedoc "Maps each session ID to the IDs of its window links and clients, and each window ID to the IDs of its window links and panes. Traverse with `related/4`; the layout is not part of the contract."
  @opaque indexes :: %{
            session_links: %{optional(String.t()) => [Ref.id()]},
            window_links: %{optional(String.t()) => [Ref.id()]},
            window_panes: %{optional(Schema.observed(String.t())) => [String.t()]},
            session_clients: %{optional(Schema.observed(String.t())) => [String.t()]}
          }
  @typedoc "Observed rows grouped by canonical entity; construction validates and deduplicates their identities."
  @type rows :: %{optional(Schema.entity()) => [map() | Schema.observation()]}
  @typedoc "Construction metadata: one server instance, ordered millisecond timestamps and explicit coverage declarations."
  @type option ::
          {:server_instance, String.t()}
          | {:captured_from, integer()}
          | {:captured_until, integer()}
          | {:fields, %{optional(Schema.entity()) => [atom()]}}
          | {:complete, [Schema.entity()]}
          | {:unavailable, %{optional(Schema.entity()) => [atom()]}}

  @typedoc "An immutable observation interval with indexed entities and explicit coverage."
  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: pos_integer(),
          server_instance: String.t(),
          captured_from: integer(),
          captured_until: integer(),
          coverage: coverage(),
          schema_version: 1,
          sessions: %{optional(String.t()) => LibTmux.Session.t()},
          windows: %{optional(String.t()) => LibTmux.Window.t()},
          window_links: %{optional(Ref.id()) => LibTmux.WindowLink.t()},
          panes: %{optional(String.t()) => LibTmux.Pane.t()},
          clients: %{optional(String.t()) => LibTmux.Client.t()},
          order: %{Schema.entity() => [Ref.id()]},
          indexes: indexes()
        }

  @doc "Validates observed rows, rejecting conflicts, invalid fields and dangling covered references."
  @spec new(rows(), [option()]) :: {:ok, t()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def new(rows, options) do
    options =
      Keyword.validate!(options, [
        :server_instance,
        :captured_from,
        :captured_until,
        :fields,
        complete: [],
        unavailable: %{}
      ])

    instance = Keyword.fetch!(options, :server_instance)
    from = Keyword.fetch!(options, :captured_from)
    until = Keyword.fetch!(options, :captured_until)

    unless is_integer(from) and is_integer(until) and from <= until,
      do: raise(ArgumentError, "capture interval must be ordered integer timestamps")

    unless match?({:ok, _}, Ref.new(:session, "$0", instance)),
      do: raise(ArgumentError, "invalid server instance")

    try do
      options = validate_declarations!(options)

      for entity <- Map.keys(rows),
          entity not in Schema.entities(),
          do: fail(:invalid_entity, [entity])

      maps =
        Map.new(Schema.entities(), fn entity ->
          {entity,
           index_rows(
             entity,
             Map.get(rows, entity, []),
             instance,
             Map.get(options[:unavailable], entity, [])
           )}
        end)

      validate_links!(maps.window_link)
      coverage = coverage(maps, options)
      validate_references!(maps, coverage)

      snapshot =
        struct!(
          __MODULE__,
          Map.merge(Map.new(@collections, fn {entity, name} -> {name, maps[entity]} end), %{
            id: System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]),
            server_instance: instance,
            captured_from: from,
            captured_until: until,
            coverage: coverage,
            order:
              Map.new(maps, fn {entity, items} ->
                {entity, items |> Map.keys() |> Enum.sort_by(&sort_key(entity, &1))}
              end),
            indexes: indexes(maps)
          })
        )

      {:ok, snapshot}
    catch
      %Error{} = error -> {:error, error}
    end
  end

  @doc "Returns plain observed items in stable identity order without loading data."
  @spec items(t(), Schema.entity_selector()) :: [Schema.observation()]
  def items(%__MODULE__{} = snapshot, entity) do
    entity = Schema.entity(entity)
    table = table(snapshot, entity)
    Enum.map(snapshot.order[entity], &Map.fetch!(table, &1))
  end

  @doc "Returns a materialized session selection without I/O."
  @spec sessions(t()) :: LibTmux.Selection.t(LibTmux.Session.t())
  def sessions(snapshot), do: LibTmux.Selection.new(snapshot, :session)
  @doc "Returns a materialized physical window selection without I/O."
  @spec windows(t()) :: LibTmux.Selection.t(LibTmux.Window.t())
  def windows(snapshot), do: LibTmux.Selection.new(snapshot, :window)
  @doc "Returns a materialized physical pane selection without I/O."
  @spec panes(t()) :: LibTmux.Selection.t(LibTmux.Pane.t())
  def panes(snapshot), do: LibTmux.Selection.new(snapshot, :pane)
  @doc "Returns a materialized membership selection without I/O."
  @spec window_links(t()) :: LibTmux.Selection.t(LibTmux.WindowLink.t())
  def window_links(snapshot), do: LibTmux.Selection.new(snapshot, :window_link)
  @doc "Returns a materialized attached-client selection without I/O."
  @spec clients(t()) :: LibTmux.Selection.t(LibTmux.Client.t())
  def clients(snapshot), do: LibTmux.Selection.new(snapshot, :client)

  @doc "Looks up one exact observed ID without I/O."
  @spec fetch(t(), Schema.entity_selector(), Ref.id()) ::
          {:ok, Schema.observation()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def fetch(%__MODULE__{} = snapshot, entity, id) do
    entity = Schema.entity(entity)

    case Map.fetch(table(snapshot, entity), id) do
      {:ok, item} ->
        {:ok, item}

      :error ->
        {:error,
         %Error{kind: :not_found, phase: :evaluation, certainty: :no_write, path: [entity, id]}}
    end
  end

  @doc "Requires a declared complete entity set, even when it has no rows."
  @spec require_complete!(t(), Schema.entity_selector()) :: :ok
  def require_complete!(snapshot, entity) do
    entity = Schema.entity(entity)

    unless snapshot.coverage.entities[entity].complete,
      do: raise_error(:entity_not_loaded, [entity])

    :ok
  end

  @doc "Requires a loaded field over the captured entity domain before evaluation."
  @spec require_field!(t(), Schema.entity_selector(), atom()) :: :ok
  def require_field!(snapshot, entity, field) do
    entity = Schema.entity(entity)
    unless Schema.field(entity, field), do: raise_error(:invalid_field, [entity, field])

    case Map.get(snapshot.coverage.entities[entity].fields, field, :unloaded) do
      :loaded -> :ok
      :unavailable -> raise_error(:field_unavailable, [entity, field])
      :unloaded -> raise_error(:field_not_loaded, [entity, field])
    end
  end

  @doc "Requires a complete relation domain, including known-empty domains."
  @spec require_relation!(t(), Schema.entity_selector(), atom(), :all | [Ref.id()]) :: :ok
  def require_relation!(snapshot, entity, relation, ids \\ :all) do
    entity = Schema.entity(entity)

    unless Map.has_key?(Schema.relations(entity), relation),
      do: raise_error(:invalid_relation, [entity, relation])

    coverage = relation_coverage(snapshot, entity, relation)
    ids = if ids == :all, do: snapshot.order[entity], else: ids

    unless coverage.loaded and Enum.all?(ids, &MapSet.member?(coverage.ids, &1)),
      do: raise_error(:relation_not_loaded, [entity, relation])

    :ok
  end

  @doc "Resolves a covered relation through captured indexes; never refreshes."
  @spec related(t(), Schema.entity_selector(), Ref.id(), atom()) ::
          Schema.observation() | nil | [Schema.observation()]
  def related(snapshot, entity, id, relation) do
    entity = Schema.entity(entity)
    require_relation!(snapshot, entity, relation, [id])
    {:ok, item} = fetch(snapshot, entity, id)
    project(snapshot, entity, item, relation)
  end

  defp index_rows(entity, rows, instance, unavailable) when is_list(rows) do
    Enum.reduce(rows, %{}, fn row, acc ->
      row = if is_struct(row), do: Map.from_struct(row), else: row
      fields = Schema.fields(entity)

      for key <- Map.keys(row),
          key != :server_instance and not Map.has_key?(fields, key),
          do: fail(:invalid_field, [entity, key])

      if Map.has_key?(row, :server_instance) and row.server_instance != instance,
        do: fail(:stale_target, [entity])

      row = if entity == :window_link, do: bind_link(row), else: row
      id = row[:id]

      unless match?({:ok, _}, Ref.new(entity, id, instance)),
        do: fail(:invalid_target, [entity, id])

      Enum.each(row, fn
        {:server_instance, _} ->
          :ok

        {_key, value} when value in [:unloaded, :unavailable] ->
          :ok

        {key, value} ->
          unless Schema.valid_value?(fields[key], value),
            do: fail(:invalid_field, [entity, id, key])
      end)

      row =
        Enum.reduce(unavailable, row, fn field, current ->
          unless Map.get(current, field, :unloaded) in [:unloaded, :unavailable],
            do: fail(:inconsistent_coverage, [entity, field])

          Map.put(current, field, :unavailable)
        end)

      row =
        if entity == :session,
          do: Map.put(row, :attached, attached(Map.get(row, :attached_count, :unloaded))),
          else: row

      item = struct!(Schema.module(entity), Map.put(row, :server_instance, instance))

      case Map.fetch(acc, id) do
        {:ok, ^item} -> acc
        {:ok, _other} -> fail(:conflicting_rows, [entity, id])
        :error -> Map.put(acc, id, item)
      end
    end)
  end

  defp bind_link(row) do
    id = {row[:session_id], row[:index], row[:window_id]}
    if Map.has_key?(row, :id) and row.id != id, do: fail(:invalid_target, [:window_link, row.id])
    Map.put(row, :id, id)
  end

  defp attached(count) when is_integer(count), do: count > 0
  defp attached(state), do: state

  defp validate_links!(links) do
    Enum.reduce(links, %{}, fn {_, link}, seen ->
      key = {link.session_id, link.index}

      if Map.has_key?(seen, key) and seen[key] != link.window_id,
        do: fail(:conflicting_link, [:window_link, link.id])

      Map.put(seen, key, link.window_id)
    end)
  end

  defp coverage(maps, options) do
    declared = Keyword.get(options, :fields, %{})
    unavailable = options[:unavailable]
    complete = options[:complete]

    for entity <- Map.keys(declared) ++ Map.keys(unavailable) ++ complete,
        entity not in Schema.entities(),
        do: fail(:invalid_entity, [entity])

    entities =
      Map.new(maps, fn {entity, items} ->
        fields = Map.get(declared, entity, [])
        missing = Map.get(unavailable, entity, [])

        for field <- fields ++ missing,
            is_nil(Schema.field(entity, field)),
            do: fail(:invalid_field, [entity, field])

        if Enum.any?(fields, &(&1 in missing)), do: fail(:inconsistent_coverage, [entity])

        fields =
          if entity == :session and :attached_count in fields,
            do: Enum.uniq([:attached | fields]),
            else: fields

        Enum.each(fields, fn field ->
          if Enum.any?(items, fn {_, item} ->
               Map.fetch!(item, field) in [:unloaded, :unavailable]
             end),
             do: fail(:inconsistent_coverage, [entity, field])
        end)

        Enum.each(missing, fn field ->
          if Enum.any?(items, fn {_, item} ->
               Map.fetch!(item, field) not in [:unloaded, :unavailable]
             end),
             do: fail(:inconsistent_coverage, [entity, field])
        end)

        states = Map.merge(Map.new(fields, &{&1, :loaded}), Map.new(missing, &{&1, :unavailable}))

        {entity,
         %{ids: MapSet.new(Map.keys(items)), complete: entity in complete, fields: states}}
      end)

    %{entities: entities}
  end

  defp validate_declarations!(options) do
    fields = Keyword.get(options, :fields, %{})
    unavailable = options[:unavailable]

    for entity <- Map.keys(fields) ++ Map.keys(unavailable) ++ options[:complete],
        entity not in Schema.entities(),
        do: fail(:invalid_entity, [entity])

    for declarations <- [fields, unavailable],
        {entity, names} <- declarations,
        name <- names,
        is_nil(Schema.field(entity, name)),
        do: fail(:invalid_field, [entity, name])

    fields = derived_coverage(fields)
    unavailable = derived_coverage(unavailable)

    for entity <- Schema.entities(),
        field <- Map.get(fields, entity, []),
        field in Map.get(unavailable, entity, []),
        do: fail(:inconsistent_coverage, [entity, field])

    options |> Keyword.put(:fields, fields) |> Keyword.put(:unavailable, unavailable)
  end

  defp derived_coverage(declarations) do
    names = Map.get(declarations, :session, [])

    if :attached in names and :attached_count not in names,
      do: fail(:inconsistent_coverage, [:session, :attached])

    if :attached_count in names,
      do: Map.put(declarations, :session, Enum.uniq([:attached | names])),
      else: declarations
  end

  defp validate_references!(maps, coverage) do
    for {entity, keys} <- @foreign_keys, {_, item} <- maps[entity], {field, target} <- keys do
      value = Map.fetch!(item, field)

      if value not in [:unloaded, :unavailable, nil] and coverage.entities[target].complete and
           not Map.has_key?(maps[target], value),
         do: fail(:inconsistent_snapshot, [entity, item.id, field])
    end
  end

  defp indexes(maps) do
    %{
      session_links: grouped(maps.window_link, :session_id, & &1.index),
      window_links: grouped(maps.window_link, :window_id, &sort_key(:window_link, &1.id)),
      window_panes: grouped(maps.pane, :window_id, &sort_key(:pane, &1.id)),
      session_clients: grouped(maps.client, :session_id, & &1.id)
    }
  end

  defp grouped(items, field, order) do
    items
    |> Map.values()
    |> Enum.group_by(&Map.fetch!(&1, field))
    |> Map.new(fn {id, rows} -> {id, rows |> Enum.sort_by(order) |> Enum.map(& &1.id)} end)
  end

  defp relation_coverage(snapshot, entity, relation) do
    {complete, required} = requirements(entity, relation)

    loaded =
      Enum.all?(complete, &snapshot.coverage.entities[&1].complete) and
        Enum.all?(required, fn {e, f} -> snapshot.coverage.entities[e].fields[f] == :loaded end)

    ids =
      if loaded,
        do:
          Enum.filter(snapshot.order[entity], fn id ->
            relation_targets_present?(snapshot, entity, id, relation)
          end),
        else: []

    %{loaded: loaded, ids: MapSet.new(ids)}
  end

  defp requirements(:pane, :window), do: {[], [pane: :window_id]}
  defp requirements(:client, :session), do: {[], [client: :session_id]}
  defp requirements(:window_link, :session), do: {[], [window_link: :session_id]}
  defp requirements(:window_link, :window), do: {[], [window_link: :window_id]}
  defp requirements(:window, :panes), do: {[:pane], [pane: :window_id]}
  defp requirements(:session, :clients), do: {[:client], [client: :session_id]}

  defp requirements(:session, :active_window),
    do:
      {[:window_link], [window_link: :session_id, window_link: :window_id, window_link: :active]}

  defp requirements(:session, :panes),
    do:
      {[:window_link, :pane],
       [window_link: :session_id, window_link: :window_id, pane: :window_id]}

  defp requirements(_entity, _relation),
    do: {[:window_link], [window_link: :session_id, window_link: :window_id]}

  defp relation_targets_present?(snapshot, :session, id, :active_window) do
    case active_link(snapshot, snapshot.sessions[id]) do
      nil -> true
      link -> Map.has_key?(snapshot.windows, link.window_id)
    end
  end

  defp relation_targets_present?(snapshot, entity, id, relation) do
    {cardinality, _target} = Schema.relations(entity)[relation]
    result = project(snapshot, entity, table(snapshot, entity)[id], relation)
    if cardinality == :one, do: not is_nil(result), else: Enum.all?(result, &(not is_nil(&1)))
  end

  defp project(s, :pane, item, :window), do: s.windows[item.window_id]
  defp project(s, :client, item, :session), do: s.sessions[item.session_id]
  defp project(s, :window_link, item, :session), do: s.sessions[item.session_id]
  defp project(s, :window_link, item, :window), do: s.windows[item.window_id]

  defp project(s, :session, item, :active_window) do
    case active_link(s, item) do
      nil -> nil
      link -> s.windows[link.window_id]
    end
  end

  defp project(s, :window, item, :panes),
    do: Enum.map(Map.get(s.indexes.window_panes, item.id, []), &s.panes[&1])

  defp project(s, :session, item, :clients),
    do: Enum.map(Map.get(s.indexes.session_clients, item.id, []), &s.clients[&1])

  defp project(s, :session, item, :window_links),
    do: Enum.map(Map.get(s.indexes.session_links, item.id, []), &s.window_links[&1])

  defp project(s, :window, item, :window_links),
    do: Enum.map(Map.get(s.indexes.window_links, item.id, []), &s.window_links[&1])

  defp project(s, :session, item, :windows),
    do:
      project(s, :session, item, :window_links)
      |> Enum.map(&s.windows[&1.window_id])
      |> Enum.uniq_by(&if(&1, do: &1.id))

  defp project(s, :window, item, :sessions),
    do:
      project(s, :window, item, :window_links)
      |> Enum.map(&s.sessions[&1.session_id])
      |> Enum.uniq_by(&if(&1, do: &1.id))
      |> Enum.sort_by(&if(&1, do: sort_key(:session, &1.id)))

  defp project(s, :session, item, :panes) do
    windows =
      project(s, :session, item, :window_links) |> Enum.map(& &1.window_id) |> MapSet.new()

    items(s, :pane) |> Enum.filter(&MapSet.member?(windows, &1.window_id))
  end

  defp table(snapshot, entity), do: Map.fetch!(snapshot, @collections[entity])

  defp active_link(snapshot, session) do
    case Enum.filter(project(snapshot, :session, session, :window_links), & &1.active) do
      [] -> nil
      [link] -> link
      _ -> raise_error(:ambiguous_relation, [:session, session.id, :active_window])
    end
  end

  defp sort_key(:window_link, {session, index, window}),
    do: {sort_key(:session, session), index, sort_key(:window, window)}

  defp sort_key(:client, id), do: id
  defp sort_key(_entity, <<_prefix, digits::binary>>), do: String.to_integer(digits)

  defp fail(kind, path),
    do: throw(%Error{kind: kind, phase: :capture, certainty: :no_write, path: path})

  defp raise_error(kind, path),
    do: raise(Error, kind: kind, phase: :evaluation, certainty: :no_write, path: path)
end

defmodule LibTmux.Transport.OneShot do
  @moduledoc """
  Executes one explicitly selected executable with bounded captured output.

  This Linux transport owns a native helper and its ordinary finite process
  tree. It never uses a shell. A worker owns the Port and observes caller
  death; the helper detects pipe closure after worker or VM death.
  Target environment entries travel as bytes to child `execve`, preserving
  empty values. The helper inherits the trusted host environment; requested
  target variables do not configure the helper. `TMUX` and `TMUX_PANE` are
  removed from the target environment.

  Limits apply per call: stdout defaults to 1 MiB, stderr to 64 KiB, and
  retained chunks to 4096. `max_total_bytes` additionally bounds both streams
  together; it defaults to their summed limits. Overload returns an error
  with a bounded prefix.
  Independent caller processes require admission limits at their host or
  server boundary; this primitive maintains no shared request queue.

  A positive timeout becomes one execution deadline. Retirement can take
  up to a separate 750 ms cleanup allowance after expiry. Missing retirement
  proof remains `:unknown`. No result authorizes replay. Helper SIGKILL,
  hostile escape and uninterruptible kernel tasks are outside the ordinary
  tree guarantee. Building the native helper requires a C11 compiler.
  """

  alias LibTmux.{Deadline, Error}
  alias LibTmux.Transport.Native
  alias LibTmux.Transport.Native.Protocol, as: NativeProtocol

  @typedoc "Captured bytes and child exit status after proven owned-process retirement; nonzero exit remains a transport result."
  @type result :: %{
          stdout: binary(),
          stderr: binary(),
          exit_status: non_neg_integer(),
          cleanup: :retired
        }

  @typedoc """
  Per-call input and capture limits; bytes and chunks are bounded independently.

  Timeout and deadline are exclusive. A supplied deadline must have at most
  600,000 ms remaining at validation; it preserves its original cutoff.
  """
  @type option ::
          {:timeout, 1..600_000}
          | {:deadline, Deadline.t()}
          | {:cwd, String.t()}
          | {:env, %{optional(binary()) => binary()}}
          | {:max_stdout_bytes | :max_stderr_bytes, 0..16_777_216}
          | {:max_total_bytes, nil | 0..33_554_432}
          | {:max_chunks, 1..65_536}

  @cleanup_ms 750
  @chunk_bytes 8192

  @doc "Runs argv without a shell, retaining exit status separately from stdout and stderr."
  @spec run(binary(), [binary()], [option()]) :: {:ok, result()} | {:error, Error.t()}
  def run(executable, arguments, options \\ []) do
    if length(options) != map_size(Map.new(options)),
      do: raise(ArgumentError, "duplicate transport options")

    if Keyword.has_key?(options, :deadline) and Keyword.has_key?(options, :timeout),
      do: raise(ArgumentError, "pass a deadline or timeout, not both")

    deadline =
      Keyword.get_lazy(options, :deadline, fn ->
        Deadline.new(Keyword.get(options, :timeout, 5000))
      end)

    options =
      Keyword.validate!(options, [
        :deadline,
        :env,
        :timeout,
        cwd: File.cwd!(),
        max_stdout_bytes: 1_048_576,
        max_stderr_bytes: 65_536,
        max_total_bytes: nil,
        max_chunks: 4096
      ])

    spec = validate(executable, arguments, options, deadline)

    if :os.type() == {:unix, :linux},
      do: run_worker(spec),
      else: {:error, %Error{kind: :unsupported_platform, phase: :spawn, certainty: :no_write}}
  end

  @doc "Runs argv, raising the same structured transport error on failure."
  @spec run!(binary(), [binary()], [option()]) :: result()
  def run!(executable, arguments, options \\ []) do
    case run(executable, arguments, options) do
      {:ok, result} -> result
      {:error, error} -> raise error
    end
  end

  defp validate(executable, arguments, options, %Deadline{} = deadline) do
    limits = %{1 => options[:max_stdout_bytes], 2 => options[:max_stderr_bytes]}

    unless Enum.all?(limits, fn {_, limit} -> is_integer(limit) and limit in 0..16_777_216 end),
      do: raise(ArgumentError, "stream limits must be 0..16 MiB")

    total_limit =
      case options[:max_total_bytes] do
        nil -> Enum.sum(Map.values(limits))
        value -> value
      end

    unless is_integer(total_limit) and total_limit in 0..33_554_432 and
             is_integer(options[:max_chunks]) and options[:max_chunks] in 1..65_536 and
             Deadline.remaining(deadline) <= 600_000 do
      raise ArgumentError,
            "limits require 0..32 MiB combined, 1..65536 chunks and at most 600000 ms"
    end

    payload =
      NativeProtocol.process(executable, arguments,
        cwd: options[:cwd],
        env: Keyword.get_lazy(options, :env, &System.get_env/0)
      )

    %{
      payload: payload,
      limits: limits,
      total_limit: total_limit,
      max_chunks: options[:max_chunks],
      deadline: deadline
    }
  end

  defp run_worker(spec) do
    caller = self()
    reply = :erlang.alias()
    token = make_ref()

    {worker, monitor} =
      spawn_monitor(fn ->
        Process.flag(:trap_exit, true)
        parent_monitor = Process.monitor(caller)
        result = execute(Map.merge(spec, %{parent_monitor: parent_monitor, token: token}))
        send(reply, {token, result})
      end)

    try do
      receive do
        {^token, result} ->
          result

        {:DOWN, ^monitor, :process, ^worker, reason} ->
          {:error,
           %Error{
             kind: :worker_failed,
             phase: :capture,
             details: %{reason: classify_exit(reason), cleanup: :unknown}
           }}
      after
        Deadline.remaining(spec.deadline) + @cleanup_ms ->
          send(worker, {:retire, token})
          {:error, %Error{kind: :timeout, phase: :retire, details: %{cleanup: :unknown}}}
      end
    after
      LibTmux.Transport.Reply.close(reply, token)
      Process.demonitor(monitor, [:flush])
    end
  end

  defp execute(spec) do
    if Deadline.remaining(spec.deadline) == 0,
      do: {:error, %Error{kind: :timeout, phase: :admission, certainty: :no_write}},
      else: open(spec)
  end

  defp open(spec) do
    case start_port(spec) do
      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}

      {:ok, port} ->
        state =
          Map.merge(spec, %{
            port: port,
            chunks: %{1 => [], 2 => []},
            bytes: %{1 => 0, 2 => 0},
            count: 0,
            started: false
          })

        try do
          remaining = Deadline.remaining(spec.deadline)

          cond do
            remaining == 0 ->
              abort(state, :timeout, :admission, %{}, :no_write)

            send_port(
              port,
              NativeProtocol.open_frame(spec.payload, input: :closed, timeout: remaining)
            ) ->
              await(state)

            true ->
              abort(state, :resource_limit, :write, %{reason: :helper_busy}, :no_write)
          end
        after
          close_port(port)
        end
    end
  end

  defp start_port(_spec) do
    {:ok,
     Port.open({:spawn_executable, Native.executable()}, [
       :binary,
       :exit_status,
       {:packet, 2}
     ])}
  rescue
    error in ErlangError ->
      {:error,
       %Error{
         kind: :launch_failed,
         phase: :spawn,
         certainty: :no_write,
         details: %{reason: classify_exit(error.original)}
       }}
  end

  defp await(state) do
    port = state.port
    parent = state.parent_monitor
    token = state.token

    receive do
      {^port, {:data, data}} ->
        frame(state, data)

      {^port, {:exit_status, status}} ->
        failure(state, :transport_closed, :capture, %{helper_status: status, cleanup: :unknown})

      {:EXIT, ^port, :normal} ->
        await(state)

      {:EXIT, ^port, reason} ->
        failure(state, :transport_closed, :capture, %{
          reason: classify_exit(reason),
          cleanup: :unknown
        })

      {:DOWN, ^parent, :process, _caller, _reason} ->
        abort(state, :cancelled, :capture)

      {:retire, ^token} ->
        abort(state, :timeout, :capture)
    after
      Deadline.remaining(state.deadline) -> abort(state, :timeout, :capture)
    end
  end

  defp frame(%{started: false} = state, <<?S, _diagnostic_pid::32>>) do
    state = %{state | started: true}
    grant(state, 1)
    grant(state, 2)
    await(state)
  end

  defp frame(%{started: true} = state, <<?D, stream, data::binary>>)
       when stream in [1, 2] and byte_size(data) in 1..@chunk_bytes do
    if state.count >= state.max_chunks do
      abort(state, :resource_limit, :capture, %{reason: :chunks})
    else
      retain(state, stream, data)
    end
  end

  defp frame(state, <<?Z, stream>>) when stream in [1, 2], do: await(state)

  defp frame(state, <<?E, reason, status::32>>) when reason in 0..3 do
    send_port(state.port, "T")
    cleanup = retire(state.port, Deadline.new(@cleanup_ms), true)

    if cleanup == :retired and reason == 0 and Deadline.remaining(state.deadline) > 0 do
      {:ok, Map.merge(capture(state), %{exit_status: status, cleanup: :retired})}
    else
      failure(
        state,
        if(reason == 2 or Deadline.remaining(state.deadline) == 0,
          do: :timeout,
          else: :transport_closed
        ),
        :capture,
        %{exit_status: status, cleanup: cleanup}
      )
    end
  end

  defp frame(state, <<?F, kind, number::32>>) when kind in 1..4 do
    if kind != 4, do: send_port(state.port, "T")
    cleanup = retire(state.port, Deadline.new(@cleanup_ms), kind != 4)

    if kind == 2,
      do: failure(state, :launch_failed, :spawn, %{errno: number, cleanup: cleanup}, :no_write),
      else:
        failure(state, :transport_failed, :capture, %{
          reason: kind,
          errno: number,
          cleanup: cleanup
        })
  end

  defp frame(state, _data), do: abort(state, :protocol_error, :parse)

  defp retain(state, stream, data) do
    stream_available = max(state.limits[stream] - state.bytes[stream], 0)
    total_available = max(state.total_limit - state.bytes[1] - state.bytes[2], 0)
    available = min(stream_available, total_available)
    retained = binary_part(data, 0, min(byte_size(data), available)) |> :binary.copy()

    state = %{
      state
      | chunks: Map.update!(state.chunks, stream, &[retained | &1]),
        bytes: Map.update!(state.bytes, stream, &(&1 + byte_size(data))),
        count: state.count + 1
    }

    if byte_size(data) > available do
      abort(state, :resource_limit, :capture, %{
        reason:
          if(total_available < stream_available,
            do: :total_bytes,
            else: if(stream == 1, do: :stdout_bytes, else: :stderr_bytes)
          )
      })
    else
      grant(state, stream)
      await(state)
    end
  end

  defp grant(state, stream) do
    available =
      min(
        state.limits[stream] - state.bytes[stream],
        state.total_limit - state.bytes[1] - state.bytes[2]
      )

    size = min(@chunk_bytes, max(available + 1, 1))
    send_port(state.port, <<?R, stream, size::16>>)
  end

  defp abort(state, kind, phase, details \\ %{}, certainty \\ :unknown) do
    send_port(state.port, "Q")
    cleanup = retire(state.port, Deadline.new(@cleanup_ms), false)
    failure(state, kind, phase, Map.put(details, :cleanup, cleanup), certainty)
  end

  defp retire(port, deadline, evidence) do
    receive do
      {^port, {:data, <<?E, _reason, _status::32>>}} ->
        send_port(port, "T")
        retire(port, deadline, true)

      {^port, {:data, <<?F, kind, _number::32>>}} when kind in 1..4 ->
        if kind != 4, do: send_port(port, "T")
        retire(port, deadline, evidence or kind != 4)

      {^port, {:data, _data}} ->
        retire(port, deadline, evidence)

      {^port, {:exit_status, _status}} ->
        if(evidence, do: :retired, else: :unknown)

      {:EXIT, ^port, :normal} ->
        retire(port, deadline, evidence)

      {:EXIT, ^port, _reason} ->
        :unknown
    after
      Deadline.remaining(deadline) -> :unknown
    end
  end

  defp capture(state) do
    %{
      stdout: state.chunks[1] |> Enum.reverse() |> IO.iodata_to_binary(),
      stderr: state.chunks[2] |> Enum.reverse() |> IO.iodata_to_binary()
    }
  end

  defp failure(state, kind, phase, details, certainty \\ :unknown) do
    {:error,
     %Error{
       kind: kind,
       phase: phase,
       certainty: certainty,
       details: Map.merge(capture(state), details)
     }}
  end

  defp send_port(port, data) do
    Port.command(port, data, [:nosuspend])
  rescue
    ArgumentError -> false
  end

  defp close_port(port) do
    if Port.info(port), do: Port.close(port)
  rescue
    ArgumentError -> :ok
  end

  defp classify_exit(reason) when is_atom(reason), do: reason
  defp classify_exit(_reason), do: :other
end
